scope: first 12 rows of the pre-existing raw audit CSV; diagnostic subset, not a new random sample or full precision estimate
reviewer: Codex source-context review; not independent human adjudication

judgments.rationale: The paper demonstrates site-directed RFpeptides designs for named targets. This is a method capability, not a no-effect binding-affinity relation.
Review describes generative scaffold methods, not measured synthesis or macrocyclization yield.

Source contrasts nitrile-to-thiazoline cyclization of C-terminal Ile versus Ala and heating versus room temperature. Proteolytic stability is the wrong endpoint; the conditional reaction observation could be useful.
Review discusses albumin association and systemic exposure, including CNS trade-offs. Exposure does not establish metabolic stability.

Local passage supports IgG1-Fc enrichment relative to avidin-coated beads. The record generalises to target proteins and its scope includes TROP2 without support in this passage; preserve the tested comparison.
Passage attributes antimicrobial modulation to irradiation of metallohelices, not merely metal coordination, and reports MIC rather than binding affinity.
Source reports in-silico affinity scores for integrin-derived blocking polypeptides; do not treat as measured affinity or cyclic-peptide SAR.
Statement concerns integrin receptor conformational rearrangement, not ligand chameleonicity.
Source reports a designed symmetric macrocycle-homodimer complex and its affinity but no contrast isolating symmetry as an affinity-enhancing intervention.
Review describes design objectives and exploration relevant to oral bioavailability; passage does not demonstrate improved bioavailability caused by macrocyclic design.
Source discusses receptor/complex solvent-accessible surface trajectories, not peptide solubility.
Review attributes limited antibacterial changes from chlorination edits to earlier SAR work. Antibacterial activity is not binding affinity; underlying primary experiment needs review.
